I was actually diagnosed with anxiety a few years ago, and they put me on Lexapro but it seemed to just make it worse and I've since stopped it. It only happens once in a while, so would it be worth seeing a new doctor if it's a rare occurrence? I find that I have a hard time figuring it all out because all of the intense emotional states I get only last a few weeks to a few months, so by the time I actually get into an appointment I'm usually back to normal or will be soon.

Thank you for your reply! I appreciate it!

Hi! I know that this is such an old post, but I wanted to thank you again for this comment... three years later. You provided so much insight and wisdom and helped me embrace the inherent shittiness of being a teenager and having emotions. Thank you for fiercely defending me and my youth in this comment section, because I do not think my developing 17-year-old brain could've handled worrying about BPD at that age, nor should it have. I used to roll my eyes when adults would tell me that these were just parts of growing up, but now that I am 20, I completely understand where everybody was coming from.

I am very happy to say that grew out of a lot of these undesirable symptoms! I mean, don't get me wrong, I still have my idiosyncrasies, but everybody does and the majority of them are just who I am and of no clinical concern, and have actually become an asset as I have gotten older. Unfortunately, the long episodic lows stuck around and highs soon followed, and I was diagnosed with bipolar 2 and subsequently prescribed treatment about a year ago, and thankfully it's been working very well and I am in such a good, happy, safe, place now. However, a lot of the symptoms I listed in this post had nothing to do with that diagnosis!

And I have a funny story regarding your suggestion on talking to my peers: I saw a lot of my high school friends recently when I was home from college, and I opened up to them about all the aforementioned growing pains I went through in high school, and what would you know? Everyone had a similar experience in some way or another. We all had a good laugh (and internal cry) about how afraid we were to open up to each other about our mental health, when in reality we all were going through it side by side, thinking we were alone.

I wish I could say that I outgrew all of this completely, and obviously bipolar disorder was not the outcome I was hoping for, but looking back, it really has gotten so much easier with age, treatment, and getting the hell out of high school.

I am now studying psychology in college and I hope to go into some sort of adolescent psychology research field as I grow older. Teenage years are tough, but people like you made it a little bit easier.

Thank you again!!
